newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Albright leaves for Washington after Czech visit.
newsitem.headline: Albright leaves for Washington after Czech visit.

text.p: U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright left the Czech Republic on Monday after a visit during which she urged Czechs to be ready for NATO membership and saw proof of her Jewish ancestry.
Albright, ending her first visit to her native Prague since starting her new job, left for Washington at about 6.25 p.m. (1625 GMT), an airport official said.

Earlier, she told a news conference she was confident the Czechs would do everything necessary to be ready for NATO membership but said they would have to modernise their armed forces and increase defence spending.
NATO last week invited the Czech Republic, Poland and Hungary to apply to join the alliance in 1999.
Albright also told Czechs they were resuming their place among European democracies "fully, finally and forever".

Albright, who says she was only recently made aware of her Jewish origins, also visited Prague's Jewish quarter on Sunday and saw the the names of her parental grandparents on the memorial walls of a synagogue dedicated to 80,000 Czechoslovak Jews who died in the Holocaust.
She said the image of the names "would for ever be seared into my heart".
